newsitem.title: UK: EUROBONDS SEE ICI SPREE WEND ITS WAY INTO FRNS.
newsitem.headline: EUROBONDS SEE ICI SPREE WEND ITS WAY INTO FRNS.

text.p: Primary market activity on Wednesday was dominated by the latest leg of British chemical giant ICI's almost unprecedented borrowing spree.
ICI raised $1.5 billion with the launch of three $500 million FRNs with maturities of 12, 15 and 18 months, taking its borrowing in the past month toward $4 billion.
Lead manager Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said there was strong demand from money managers and treasury funds in the Far East and London looking for short-dated paper yielding above LIBOR.
Paper was being sold in size with at least one buyer of $50 million ticket amid ticket sizes of $20-$30 million.
"People are subscribing on the basis of the company's story that it plans to return to being a solid single-A credit," a syndicate manager at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.
ICI, rated Baa1 by Moodys and A- by S&P, was downgraded ealier this year by both ratings agencies after its $8 billion acquisition of Unilever's speciality chemicals business.
Today's three issues all pay three-month LIBOR plus 6.25 basis points. The longer-dated deals are callable at par on coupon dates from September 1998.
They were ICI's fourth visit to the international bond market in under a month as it refinanced loans taken out after the Unilever deal.
ICI made a start on that debt in early July by selling half its bulk chemical operations to U.S. chemicals giant DuPont for $3 billion.
The four public deals since have totalled around $2.6 billion. ICI has also raised around $800 million in the MTN market and issued CP in the same period, dealers said.

"The fact that they have raised so much so quickly should be seen a positive factor," one new issues trader said. "That they could move so quickly after the Unilver deal is a great sign of market confidence."

Elsewhere, the junk bond deal expected from Central European Media will be in two tranches, a $100 million seven-year and a 100 million mark seven-year, priced to yield 300-325 b.p. over respective government bond markets
The Morgan Stanley-led notes have been rated B1/B+.
"Much of this is market-driven," said one source close to the offering. "We want to make sure (the issues) will be sufficiently liquid."
Central European Media owns and operates national and regional private television stations in Germany, Poland, the Czech Republic, the Slovak Republic, Slovenia and Romania.
